details.description: gemini-flash-lite-latest is Google's rolling alias for the current release of its Gemini Flash-Lite-tier model on the Gemini Developer API, rather than a fixed, dated model. Google's Gemini API documentation describes a 'latest' name as pointing 'to the latest release for a specific model variation', an alias that 'will get hot-swapped with every new release of a specific model variation'; Google gives at least two weeks' email notice before a breaking change to the model behind the alias. As of 24 September 2026, Google's Gemini API models page lists Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite as the newest stable Flash-Lite-tier release, though Google does not publish an explicit statement that the alias currently names that exact snapshot.
advantages: Always resolves to Google's current release for the Flash-Lite variation, so applications keep getting model improvements without changing the model string, per Google's Gemini API documentation.
Google commits to at least two weeks' email notice before a breaking change to the model behind the alias, per Google's Gemini API documentation.
disadvantages: Because the alias is hot-swapped with each new release, the exact underlying model version, and its behavior and benchmark scores, can change without any corresponding change to application code, per Google's Gemini API documentation.
Google's own naming-convention guidance recommends most production apps use a specific stable model string rather than a rolling alias like this one.
use_cases: High-throughput, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification or translation at the Flash-Lite tier's cost point
Development and prototyping that should always track Google's newest Flash-Lite release without needing to update the model string

notes: This id names a moving-target alias, not a fixed model, so no benchmark page reports scores for 'gemini-flash-lite-latest' itself; evaluations was left empty rather than borrowing scores from whichever dated model it currently resolves to. Catalog facts (1,048,576 input / 65,536 output tokens, audio+image+text input, text output) match every recent Gemini 3.x Flash-Lite model, including the current newest stable release Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, whose own model card gives the same 'up to 1M' input / '64K' output figures plus video file input (not in the catalog's modality list). The deprecations page does not list gemini-flash-lite-latest as a separately tracked model id, consistent with it being a rolling alias rather than a pinned release.
